The snow came early that year, and it came into the house through the cracks in the wall. Jurgis sat at the table with his coat on, watching his wife stir the pot, which held nothing but water and a few shreds of cabbage. The children had gone to bed hungry again; he could hear the youngest coughing, a thin dry sound that went on and on. He had worked sixteen hours that day, standing in slush up to his ankles, and his hands were so numb that he could scarcely hold the spoon. “It will get better,” he said, but she did not turn around. Outside the wind rose, and the lamp flickered, and the whole wretched room seemed to shrink around them.
